props.gloss_en: a fish that has scales now and will shed them when it rises from the water (akunas, afunas, kesaftiyas, akhsaftiyas, atunas) is permitted
whatever has scales has fins; and there is what has fins and has no scales
it has scales and it has fins -- a kosher fish
it has fins and no scales -- a non-kosher fish
the verse writes both 'fins and scales' as the sign of a kosher fish (Lev 11:9)
kaskeset is a garment [scales], as it is written: 'and he was clad with a coat of kaskasim' (I Sam 17:5)
'to make Torah great and glorious' (Isa 42:21) -- [fins are written although scales suffice]
from 'eat what has [fins and scales]' I hear 'do not eat what has not', and from 'do not eat what has not' I hear 'eat what has' -- each verse implies the other
why did it teach both? to transgress on its account a positive and a negative command
the verse clause 'these may you eat of all that are in the waters' (Lev 11:9)
[one might think:] since it permitted explicitly and permitted implicitly -- as the explicit permission is only in vessels, so the implicit is only in vessels
whence to include pits, ditches and caves, that one bends and drinks from them and does not refrain? the verse says 'these may you eat of all that are in the waters'
in seas and rivers, with [signs] eat, without do not; but in vessels, even without -- eat (from the 'has' verse, Lev 11:9)
say instead: in vessels, even if it has [signs], do not eat
as it is written: 'and all that have not fins and scales in the seas and in the rivers' -- but in vessels, even without, eat (Lev 11:10)
say: 'in the waters' is a generalisation, 'in the seas and rivers' a detail -- the generalisation holds only the detail: seas and rivers yes, channels and trenches no
'in the waters' -- it generalised again: generalisation, detail, generalisation
wherever you find two generalisations adjacent to each other, place the detail between them and expound them as generalisation, detail, generalisation
as the detail is explicitly flowing water, so all flowing water
what does it include? trenches and channels -- to forbid [their creatures without fins and scales]
say: as the detail is water on the ground, so all water on the ground -- including even pits, ditches and caves, to forbid; excluding only vessels
'in the waters' twice is not generalisation and detail but amplification and restriction: amplified, restricted, amplified again -- it amplified everything
say: it includes pits, ditches and caves, to forbid; and excludes only vessels
I could reverse it: pits, ditches and caves forbidden; trenches and channels permitted
I include pits, ditches and caves, which are enclosed like vessels, and I exclude trenches and channels, which are not enclosed like vessels
the 'has' verse is the explicit [permission in vessels], the 'has not' verse the implicit
the 'has not' verse is the explicit, the 'has' verse the implicit
a person should not filter beer through straw at night
lest [a creature] separate above the straw and fall back into the cup, and he transgresses 'the swarming thing that swarms upon the earth'
there [onto the vessel's side] -- that is its [normal] growth
'every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth' -- to include gnats that one filtered
the reason is that he filtered them; but if he did not filter them -- permitted
a cucumber that became wormy while attached is forbidden, because of 'the swarming thing that swarms upon the earth'
'upon the earth' -- to exclude the zizin in lentils, the gnats in kelisim, and the worm in dates and dried figs
'every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth' -- to include the worm in the roots of olive trees and of vines
no: both are while attached, and no difficulty: this one in the fruit, that one in the tree itself
[a worm] that separated and died -- what is the law?
[if] part of it [separated] -- what is the law?
[if it separated] into the open air -- what is the law?
[if it went] onto the top of the date -- what is the law?
onto the top of its pit -- what is the law?
from date to date -- what is the law?
kukyanei [worms in an animal's organs] are forbidden
what is the reason? they come from outside
if they came from outside, they would be found by way of the digestive tract
kukyanei are permitted
what is the reason? they grow from it [the animal]
what is the reason? it sleeps, and worms enter it through its snout
worms of meat are forbidden
[worms] of fish are permitted
Ravina said to his mother: absorb [it] for me and I will eat
'and their carcasses you shall detest' -- to include the worms in an animal

an animal becomes permitted by slaughter, and these [worms], since slaughter does not work for them, remain forbidden; but fish become permitted by mere gathering, and these, when they grow, grow in permittedness
'goes upon the belly' -- the snake; 'whatever' -- to include the earthworm and what resembles it
'upon all fours' -- the scorpion; 'whatever goes' -- to include the beetle and what resembles it
'has many feet' -- the centipede; 'even all' -- to include what resembles it and what resembles that
the leviathan is a kosher fish
'his pride is his rows of shields' (Job 41:7) -- these are its scales
'sharpest potsherds are under him' (Job 41:22) -- these are the fins with which it swims
